questions.question: A sum becomes two times in 4 years at a certain rate of simple interest. Find the time (in years) in which the same amount will be seven times at the same rate of interest.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum becomes two times in 4 years at a certain rate of simple interest.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest formula: A = P(1 + rt)

Where A is the amount, P is the principal, r is the rate of interest per year, and t is the time in years.

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P and the rate of interest be r.

After 4 years, the amount becomes 2P.

Using the simple interest formula:

2P = P(1 + 4r)

⇒ 2 = 1 + 4r

⇒ 4r = 1

⇒ r = 1/4

We need to find the time (t) in which the amount becomes seven times the principal (7P):

Using the simple interest formula again:

7P = P(1 + rt)

⇒ 7 = 1 + (1/4)t

⇒ 7 - 1 = (1/4)t

⇒ 6 = (1/4)t

⇒ t = 6 × 4

⇒ t = 24

**The time in which the same amount will be seven times at the same rate of interest is 24 years.**

questions.question: Namita deposited ₹9,000 which amounted to ₹10,200 after 3 years at simple interest per annum. Had the interest been 2% more, what amount (in ₹) would she get?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹9,000

Amount (A) = ₹10,200

Time (T) = 3 years

Simple Interest (SI) = A - P = ₹10,200 - ₹9,000 = ₹1,200

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100

New Simple Interest Rate = Old Rate + 2%

New Amount = Principal + New Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

Let's find the old interest rate first:

⇒ ₹1,200 = (₹9,000 × R × 3) / 100

⇒ 120,000 = 27,000R

⇒ R = 120,000 / 27,000

⇒ R = 40/9%

New Interest Rate = 40/9% + 2% = 58/9%

New Simple Interest:

⇒ SI = (₹9,000 × 58/9 × 3) / 100

⇒ SI = ₹1,740

New Amount:

⇒ A = ₹9,000 + ₹1,740

⇒ A = ₹10,740

**The amount Namita would get if the interest rate had been 2% more is ₹10,740.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹14400

Rate of Interest (R) = 11% per annum

Time (T) = 12 months = 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5bc60331c3848a052b6cd507d1869333904a436b29f022eac043deaedf4c1153.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = (14400 × 11 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 144 × 11

⇒ SI = 1584

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1584.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount received at the end of the period is the sum of the Principal and Simple Interest: A = P + SI.

Fractional Time Periods

If time is given in months, it must be converted to years by dividing by 12. If time is given in days, divide by 365 (or 366 in leap years) before applying the standard formula.

Simple vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal. Compound interest is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

Rule of 72

A quick mental math shortcut to estimate how long it takes an investment to double in value is to divide 72 by the annual interest rate (Time ≈ 72 ÷ R).

questions.question: If a certain sum of money becomes double of itself in 11 years 6 months at simple interest, then what will be the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money doubles itself in 11 years 6 months at simple interest.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

Since the sum doubles, SI = Principal

So, Principal = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

**Calculation:**

Time = 11 years 6 months = 11.5 years

Let the Principal be P.

SI = P

P = (P × Rate × 11.5) / 100

⇒ 1 = (Rate × 11.5) / 100

⇒ Rate = 100 / 11.5

⇒ Rate = 8.69%

**The annual rate of interest is 8.69%.**

Amount = 5P

To become 12 time of P

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 5808 after 2 years and to Rs. 7,320 after 5 years at the same rate percent per annum at simple interest. What will be the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 8,500 for 4dfrac{2}{3} years at the same rate?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amounts after 2 years = Rs. 5808

Amounts after 5 years = Rs. 7320

Rate of interest is same in both cases.

**Formula used:**

P = A – S.I

A = P + S.I

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

R = (S.I × 100)/(P × T)

Where P = Principal, A = Amount, S.I = Simple Interest,

R = Rate of interest, T = Time period

**Calculation:**

Amounts after 5 years - Amounts after 2 years = 7320 - 5808

⇒ (P + S.I₅) - (P + S.I₂) = 1512

⇒ P + (P × R × 5)/100 - P - (P × R × 2)/100 = 1512

⇒ [(P × R)/100](5 - 2) = 1512

⇒ (P × R × 3)/100 = 1512

⇒ (P × R × 2)/100 = 1512 × (2/3)

⇒ (P × R × 2)/100 = 1008

Interest in 2 years = Rs. 1008

Interest in 1 year = Rs. (1008/2)

⇒ Rs. 504

Principal = Amount – S.I

⇒ Rs. 5808 - Rs. 1008

⇒ Rs. 4800

R = (S.I × 100)/(P × T)

⇒ (504 × 100)/(4800 × 1)

⇒ 504/48

⇒ 21/2%

Now P = 8500, R = 21/2%, T = 4(2)/(3) years = 14/3 years

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ [8500 × (21/2) × (14/3)]/100

⇒ (8500 × 21 × 14)/(100 × 2 × 3)

⇒ (85 × 21 × 14)/6

⇒ 4165

∴ The simple interest on a sum of Rs.8,500 for 4(2)/(3) years at the rate of (21/2)% will be Rs. 4165.
